# eval corpus — experiment output, not reference material

**Every markdown file under this directory was generated by a language model to measure a writing
instruction. None of it was written to be correct, and none of it was fact-checked as documentation.
Some of it is wrong. Do not read it as a guide to anything.**

536 answers across six runs. Each file's front matter says which run, variant, replicate, task, and
model produced it, and repeats the warning above.

## Why the errors are still here

Twenty answers in `run-1/` carry a `reviewerFinding` block naming a specific technical error, its
severity, and which reviewer caught it — for example:

```yaml
reviewerFinding:
  severity: major
  foundBy: "opus"
  error: "Claims a resolver hoists one version and gives it to a package whose declared
    range excludes it. Resolvers nest a second copy instead."
```

Those errors are **not defects in the corpus. They are the corpus.** The finding they support is that
instruction wording moves length and vocabulary by 2–3x and does not move factual accuracy at all —
which can only be shown by keeping the wrong answers next to the right ones, with the instruction
that produced each. Fixing them would delete the evidence.

Only run 1 was fact-checked, so an unannotated file is *unreviewed*, not *verified*. Runs 2–5 and the
Sonnet transfer check have no accuracy data at all, by design: `eval/README.md` records that accuracy
is a separate system with a separate trigger, and re-running reviewers on an instruction change
measures nothing.

## Why front matter is safe here

Annotating an answer must not change its score, or the corpus stops being evidence.

It does not. Verified before the migration: 15 answers scored identically with and without a front
matter block, across composite, word count, complex-word count, and every dimension.
`mdast-util-to-nlcst` does not treat front matter as text content. `eval/score.mjs` and
`eval/emit-results.mjs` both read these files directly and reproduce the published numbers.

## What this is for

Scores are frozen at the version that produced them; answers are not. Keeping the prose is what makes
these questions answerable later:

- **Did the engine change, or did the instruction stop landing?** Answered on 2026-08-08 by
  re-scoring run 2 at 0.4.2 against means recorded at 0.3.0 — all four gated metrics reproduced to
  the decimal, and only the ungated composite moved. That check needed the prose.
- **What would a new dimension have said about an old run?** Only askable while the old run exists.
- **Does a finding survive a re-score after a scoring change?** Same.

`eval/results/run-*.json` holds the scores for every answer here, stamped with the engine version
that produced them. Re-emit after an upgrade to get a second file and diff it; do not overwrite.

## Layout

| directory | run | date | model | n |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run-1/` | 1 | 2026-08-02 | claude-opus-5 | 56 |
| `run-2/` | 2 | 2026-08-02 | claude-opus-5 | 90 |
| `run-3/` | 3 | 2026-08-03 | claude-opus-5 | 90 |
| `run-4/` | 4 | 2026-08-03 | claude-opus-5 | 90 |
| `run-sonnet/` | transfer | 2026-08-03 | claude-sonnet-5 | 90 |
| `run-5/` | 5 | 2026-08-08 | claude-opus-5 | 120 |

Filenames are `<variant>-<rep>-<task>.md`. The three fields are dash-separated and never contain
dashes themselves — that filename is the only thing carrying the experimental design.

Variants are defined in `eval/variants.md`, tasks in `eval/tasks.md`.
